items.p: What is the job market?
items.a: The market where businesses that need employees and people looking for work interact
w: The market where companies sell their products
A place where people buy shares
items.ref: Job market: the market where there is an interaction between businesses that need employees and individuals who are looking for work.

items.p: What is a tight job market?
items.a: There are many job offers but few people looking for work
w: There are more people looking for work than jobs
There are no job offers at all
items.ref: Tight: there are many job offers but few people looking for work.

items.p: What happens during recessions?
items.a: Unemployment rises and wages are low
items.ref: During recessions, unemployment rises and there is economic stagnation, with a low level of wages.

items.p: What do many employers prefer today?
items.a: People with the right skills, rather than only qualifications
w: Only people with many years of experience
Only people with a university degree
People who do not want to learn
items.ref: Many employers prefer hiring people with the necessary skills to perform current tasks and adapt rapidly to new challenges.

items.p: Why are there many job vacancies?
items.a: Ageing population, less immigration and fewer people accepting low-wage jobs
items.ref: This situation is due to an ageing population, a decline in immigration and a change in attitude towards work.

items.p: How was work in the past?
items.a: People had long-term stable jobs with the same employer
items.ref: In the past people had long-term stable jobs with the same employer.

items.p: What is the gig economy?
items.a: Jobs that last a specific length of time, like freelance work
w: Jobs in the music industry only
Jobs for life in big companies
items.ref: The gig economy refers to jobs lasting a specific length of time: freelancers, independent contractors, temporary hires.

items.p: Which is an example of a gig job without specific qualifications?
items.a: Food delivery
items.ref: It ranges from professional services to jobs that do not require specific qualifications, like food delivery services.

items.p: Which is an advantage of gig work?
items.a: Flexibility and a better work-life balance
items.ref: Gig workers can choose the types of jobs they do, when and where they do them: work-life balance.

items.p: Which is a disadvantage of gig work?
items.a: Modest pay and no benefits
items.ref: Gig workers don't have the protection of minimum wages, health insurance and trade unions.

items.p: What made it possible to work anywhere and at any time?
items.a: Digital devices
items.ref: Thanks to digital devices, it is possible to work anywhere and at any time.

items.p: What changed the vision of remote working?
items.a: The Covid-19 pandemic
items.ref: The Covid-19 pandemic completely changed this vision: flexible work patterns are now the norm.

items.p: What is job sharing?
items.a: Two people share one full-time job, each working part-time
items.ref: Job sharing: when two people share one full-time job, each one working part-time.

items.p: What is a condensed work week?
items.a: Working longer hours on fewer days
items.ref: Condensed work week: for example, four days of 10 hours instead of five days of 8 hours.

items.p: What do almost half of Gen Z employees prefer?
items.a: A hybrid model, combining remote and office work
items.ref: Almost half of them prefer a hybrid model; full remote work may make them feel isolated.

items.p: Where does digital communication take place?
items.a: Internally among staff and externally with customers
items.ref: It takes place both internally among staff and externally with customers.

items.p: Which is a main form of digital communication?
items.a: Video conferencing
items.ref: Its main forms are emails, instant messaging, live chat, video conferencing and project management tools.

items.p: What is the main feature of digital communication?
items.a: Information is transmitted instantaneously
w: It works only in one country
items.ref: The main feature of digital communication is that information is transmitted instantaneously.

items.p: Who invented the Zoom app in 2011?
items.a: Eric Yuan
items.ref: The Zoom app was invented in 2011 by Eric Yuan, a former vice president of Cisco.

items.p: What led to Zoom's explosive growth?
items.a: The Covid-19 pandemic
items.ref: It was the Covid-19 pandemic that led to the company's explosive growth.

items.p: What are employability skills?
items.a: Qualities that make a person attractive for employment
items.ref: Employability skills: qualities and attributes making an individual attractive for employment and successful in the workplace.

items.p: What is the advantage of soft skills compared to hard skills?
items.a: They can be applied in real-world situations
w: They are learnt only at school
items.ref: Their main advantage is that they can be applied in practical circumstances and in real-world situations.

items.p: Which are the three types of employability skills?
items.a: How you work, how you work with others, how you think
w: How you eat, sleep and study
How you dress, speak and walk
How you buy, sell and save
items.ref: They can be divided into three types: how you work, how you work with others, how you think.

items.p: What does 'working to deadlines' mean?
items.a: Prioritising and planning, being reliable
items.ref: Working to deadlines: prioritizing and planning, reliability.

items.p: What does negotiation mean?
items.a: Looking for ideas that benefit everybody: give and take
items.ref: Negotiation: looking for ideas benefitting all, 'give and take'.
